To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a stochastic multi-fluid transport model is derived for intermediate-energy heavy ion collisions and that the model is applied to study fluctuation phenomena in a two-fluid scenario.

the Boltzmann-Langvin equation for the relativistic Boltzman transport equation (RBE) is reduced to a multi-fluid model and that the corresponding transport coefficients (interfluid friction force and interfluid diffusion tensor) are extracted and applied to the study of fluctuations in the equilibrating process of two counter-streaming fluid elements.

the interfluid diffusion tensor and the interfluid friction force are determined by the collisional relaxation times and the mean-free-path length of the fluids and that the interfluid friction is proportional to the difference in the mean flow velocities of the fluids and inversely proportional to the mean-free-path lengths of the fluids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stochastic dynamics of the relativistic fluid in the presence of fluctuations.
stochastic models of relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
the following questions: (1) What are the transport coefficients in a relativistic multi-fluid model?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Langevin approach to the Boltzmann equation is not a viable approach to the problem of the Boltzmann-Langmuir equation.
the stochastic multi-fluid model is a good candidate for describing fluctuation phenomena in heavy-ion collisions.
, for the case of the Boltzmann-Lagrangian equation, the fluctuating forces and diffusion coefficients are of the same order of magnitude as the mean-field forces and the diffusion coefficients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Boltzmann equation with a stochastic collision term is equivalent to the multi-fluid model with a stochastic source.
the interflow friction and diffusion coefficients are the key to understanding the stochastic multi-fluid model.

we have shown how to derive a stochastic multi-fluid equation from the relativistic Boltz- mann-Langevin equation and how to calculate the transport coefficients in the relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interflow diffusion is the dominant contribution to fluctuations.
the interflow diffusion is a crucial ingredient to describe the fluctuation-dissipation relation in the equilibrating fluid.
the interflow friction and the interflow viscosity are the two most important transport coefficients that govern the equilibration of nuclear matter.
